# sokrypton/colabfoldsparkPowered by Gemini

# sokrypton/colabfoldsparkPowered by Gemini

Updated onJul 14, 2026Commit[`d04bf9c`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/tree/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b)Gemini can make mistakes, so double\-check it\.![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The ColabFold repository provides a pipeline for predicting protein structures and complexes\. It integrates AlphaFold models with MMseqs2 for multiple sequence alignment \(MSA\) generation\. This pipeline covers environment setup, input data handling, model execution, and result analysis\.

 The pipeline orchestrates the prediction workflow through [pyproject\.toml L56](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/pyproject.toml#L56)\. It manages the entire process from argument parsing and environment setup to result analysis and output file management\. This includes generating multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\) and templates, engineering features for AlphaFold models, and executing iterative structure predictions\. The system supports batch processing for multiple sequences and integrates functionalities for AlphaFold3\. For details on the overall workflow, refer to [Overall Workflow and Batch Processing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#protein-structure-prediction-pipeline-overall-workflow-and-batch-processing)\.

 Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) and template generation are critical preliminary steps, leveraging MMseqs2 to search biological databases\. AlphaFold models then use this evolutionary information to predict 3D protein structures and complexes\. The system manages AlphaFold model weights, configures execution parameters, and optimizes model loading and compilation for efficient prediction\. More information on MSA generation is available in [MSA and Template Generation with MMseqs2](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#msa-and-template-generation-with-mmseqs2), and model specifics in [AlphaFold Model Configuration and Execution](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#alphafold-model-configuration-and-execution)\.

 Predicted structures include confidence scores such as pLDDT and Predicted Aligned Error \(PAE\)\. The pipeline provides tools for visualizing these metrics, alongside interactive 3D representations of protein structures\. It supports various input data formats and includes utilities for tasks such as converting DeepFold model weights and setting up a local MSA server\. For output analysis, see [Visualization and Output Analysis](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#protein-structure-prediction-pipeline-visualization-and-output-analysis), and for local server setup, refer to [Local MSA Server Setup and Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#local-msa-server-setup-and-management)\.## Protein Structure Prediction Pipeline

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The ColabFold repository provides a protein structure prediction pipeline that integrates AlphaFold with MMseqs2 to predict protein structures and complexes\. This pipeline covers the workflow from input preparation and multiple sequence alignment \(MSA\) generation to model execution, result analysis, and visualization\. It supports batch processing of multiple protein sequences and has integrated functionalities for AlphaFold3\.

 The core functionality is orchestrated by [pyproject\.toml L56](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/pyproject.toml#L56), which manages argument parsing, environment setup, and the sequential execution of various stages\. This includes MSA and template generation, which are critical for providing context to the prediction models\. MMseqs2 is used for this purpose, searching against databases to identify homologous sequences and known structural templates\. The pipeline also handles feature engineering, transforming raw sequence and alignment data into the fixed\-size inputs required by AlphaFold models\.

 After input preparation, the pipeline proceeds with iterative structure prediction, where AlphaFold models generate 3D coordinates along with confidence scores such as pLDDT and Predicted Aligned Error \(PAE\)\. The results are then analyzed and visualized, with tools for plotting confidence metrics and displaying 3D protein structures, including options for coloring and structural alignment\. Output files, including PDBs and JSONs, are robustly managed\.

 The system supports batch processing, allowing users to efficiently predict structures for multiple protein sequences or complexes\. It also includes specific integrations for AlphaFold3, facilitating the generation of compatible input dictionaries and handling various molecule types beyond proteins for broader molecular complex prediction\. Details on the complete batch processing workflow can be found in [Overall Workflow and Batch Processing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#protein-structure-prediction-pipeline-overall-workflow-and-batch-processing)\. The repository also includes a local MSA server setup for efficient and scalable MSA generation, as described in [Local MSA Server Setup and Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#local-msa-server-setup-and-management)\.### Overall Workflow and Batch Processing

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [pyproject\.toml L56](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/pyproject.toml#L56) utility orchestrates a comprehensive pipeline for protein structure prediction, designed to handle multiple queries efficiently\. Its workflow begins with argument parsing and environmental setup\. The [batch\.py L1771](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1771) function in [`colabfold/batch.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py) configures prediction parameters, such as the MSA \(Multiple Sequence Alignment\) mode, use of templates, and AlphaFold model types, and then initializes logging and environment variables like [AlphaFold2\.ipynb L314](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/AlphaFold2.ipynb#L314) and [AlphaFold2\.ipynb L316](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/AlphaFold2.ipynb#L316) to optimize memory usage for the JAX framework\.

 A critical step involves generating MSAs and identifying structural templates\. The [batch\.py L648](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L648) function, also within [`colabfold/batch.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py), determines whether to perform these searches, leveraging external tools like MMseqs2 \(via [colabfold\.py L66](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L66) in [`colabfold/colabfold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/colabfold.py)\)\. This process supports various MSA modes and can create mock templates if none are found\. The pipeline also includes functionalities for creating HHsearch databases from custom PDB/CIF files using [batch\.py L280](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L280) and [batch\.py L222](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L222), which perform necessary file conversions and validations\. For a more detailed understanding of MSA and template generation, refer to [MSA and Template Generation with MMseqs2](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#msa-and-template-generation-with-mmseqs2)\.

 Following MSA and template generation, raw biological data undergoes feature engineering to be compatible with AlphaFold models\. Functions like [batch\.py L879](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L879), [batch\.py L802](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L802), and [batch\.py L815](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L815) in [`colabfold/batch.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py) transform the input into [mock\.py L13](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L13) objects, handling both monomeric and multimeric cases\. Dynamic padding, managed by [batch\.py L343](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L343), optimizes JAX compilation by ensuring consistent input lengths, thus reducing recompilation overhead for sequences of varying sizes\. This process is further elaborated in [AlphaFold Input Feature Engineering and Preprocessing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#alphafold-model-configuration-and-execution-alphafold-input-feature-engineering-and-preprocessing)\.

 The core of the pipeline is the iterative structure prediction process managed by [batch\.py L394](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L394) in [`colabfold/batch.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py)\. This function iterates through multiple random seeds and AlphaFold models, processing input features and executing the prediction\. It calculates confidence scores such as [batch\.py L491](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L491), [ESMFold\.ipynb L177](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/ESMFold.ipynb#L177), [AlphaFold2\.ipynb L247](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/AlphaFold2.ipynb#L247), and [AlphaFold2\.ipynb L247](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/AlphaFold2.ipynb#L247), providing metrics for evaluating model quality\.

 Finally, the pipeline handles output files robustly\. It saves unrelaxed PDB structures, optionally performs Amber relaxation on top\-ranked predictions via [relax\.py L3](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/relax.py#L3), and generates JSON files with confidence scores and various plots \(MSA coverage, pAE, pLDDT, etc\.\)\. A [batch\.py L377](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L377) class within [`colabfold/batch.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py) organizes output files with consistent naming conventions\. The pipeline also supports generating input files specifically formatted for AlphaFold3 using [batch\.py L1705](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1705), enabling compatibility with newer model versions\. For more on output analysis and visualization, see [Visualization and Output Analysis](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#protein-structure-prediction-pipeline-visualization-and-output-analysis), and for AlphaFold3 specific integrations, refer to [AlphaFold3 Specific Integrations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#protein-structure-prediction-pipeline-alphafold3-specific-integrations)\.### Input Data Handling and Homooligomerization

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

ColabFold supports a variety of input data formats, including FASTA, A3M, CSV, TSV, PDB, and CIF files\. Sequences are extracted from these files, and within complex inputs, molecules are classified as either protein or non\-protein types \(e\.g\., SMILES strings\)\. For multi\-chain predictions, Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) are paired and padded to ensure consistency\.

 The system handles the expansion of MSAs and deletion matrices to accurately model both homooligomeric and heterooligomeric protein complexes\. This involves replicating MSAs for individual homooligomeric components and intelligently copying sequence fragments to appropriate homooligomeric copies within heterooligomeric contexts\. This functionality is crucial for preparing input features for AlphaFold models, ensuring that multimeric predictions accurately reflect the biological assembly\.### Visualization and Output Analysis

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

ColabFold provides a suite of tools for visualizing and analyzing protein structure prediction results, offering insights into model quality and structural features\. This includes functions for generating various plots and for interactive 3D visualization of protein structures\.

 Confidence scores and errors are depicted through several plot types\. Predicted Local Distance Difference Test \(pLDDT\) plots, for instance, are generated by functions such as [colabfold\.py L378](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L378) and [colabfold\.py L520](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L520) in [`colabfold/colabfold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/colabfold.py), which display the per\-residue confidence of the predicted structures\. A legend for pLDDT scores is available through [colabfold\.py L352](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L352) in the same file\. Predicted Aligned Error \(PAE\) maps, which indicate the expected error in the inter\-residue distance after optimal rigid\-body superposition, are created using [colabfold\.py L537](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L537) or [colabfold\.py L635](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/colabfold.py#L635) in [`colabfold/colabfold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/colabfold.py) and [plot\.py L4](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/plot.py#L4) in [`colabfold/plot.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/plot.py)\. These plots are particularly useful for assessing the relative domain orientations and interface confidence in protein complexes\. Additional structural metrics, such as adjacency matrices and distance matrices, can be visualized via [colabfold\.py L549](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L549) and [colabfold\.py L561](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L561) in [`colabfold/colabfold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/colabfold.py)\.

 Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) coverage and identity are visualized to understand the quality of the evolutionary information used for prediction\. Functions like [colabfold\.py L406](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L406) in [`colabfold/colabfold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/colabfold.py) and [plot\.py L20](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/plot.py#L20) in [`colabfold/plot.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/plot.py) display these aspects, with [plot\.py L20](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/plot.py#L20) supporting multi\-chain inputs\.

 For 3D visualization of protein structures, ColabFold integrates [pyproject\.toml L34](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/pyproject.toml#L34)\. The [pdb\.py L1](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/pdb.py#L1) function in [`colabfold/colabfold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/colabfold.py) and [`colabfold/pdb.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/pdb.py) allows interactive viewing of PDB files\. Structures can be colored based on different properties, such as pLDDT confidence \(where red indicates low confidence and blue indicates high confidence\), a rainbow gradient from N\-terminus to C\-terminus, or by individual chain\. Options are available to display sidechains and mainchains, and to adjust confidence thresholds for coloring\. The [colabfold\.py L659](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L659) function in [`colabfold/colabfold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/colabfold.py) provides a high\-level interface to plot protein backbone structures, optionally orienting them for optimal viewing using [colabfold\.py L790](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/colabfold.py#L790), which can weight the orientation by pLDDT scores\. Structural alignment is performed using the [colabfold\.py L576](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L576) algorithm, implemented in [`colabfold/colabfold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/colabfold.py), to superimpose structures for comparison\. Furthermore, the [colabfold\.py L587](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L587) function in [`colabfold/colabfold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/colabfold.py) offers a 2D projection of a 3D trace, coloring segments by properties like N\-C gradient, pLDDT, or chain, and applying shading for depth perception\.

 Advanced structural metrics, particularly for protein complexes, are computed and visualized by modules in [`colabfold/alphafold`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold)\. This includes [extra\_ptm\.py L42](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L42), [extra\_ptm\.py L206](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L206), and [extra\_ptm\.py L221](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L221) from [`colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py) which calculate variants of predicted TM\-score for inter\-chain and intra\-chain analysis\. These metrics, alongside [extra\_ptm\.py L270](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L270), can be visualized using matrix plots generated by [extra\_ptm\.py L331](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L331) and [extra\_ptm\.py L414](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L414) in [`colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py), providing a detailed view of interactions within predicted complexes\. See [AlphaFold Model Configuration and Execution](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#alphafold-model-configuration-and-execution) for more details\.### Management of AlphaFold Parameters and Citations

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

AlphaFold model parameters, which include weights and configurations, are managed through a structured download and loading process\. The primary mechanism for obtaining these parameters is handled by the [download\.py L38](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/download.py#L38) function in [`colabfold/download.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/download.py)\. This function retrieves model weights from remote sources like Google Cloud Storage or a content delivery network \(CDN\)\. It supports various AlphaFold model types, including different multimer versions and specialized models\. The download process is designed to be robust, incorporating progress tracking for user feedback and error handling for download failures\. It also employs an idempotency check, using a success marker to prevent unnecessary re\-downloads of already acquired parameters\. For models that consist of multiple individual files, such as [AlphaFold2\.ipynb L235](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/AlphaFold2.ipynb#L235), the utility can perform parallel downloads to improve efficiency\.

 Once downloaded, model parameters are loaded and optimized for efficient prediction, as detailed in [AlphaFold Model Loading and JIT Compilation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#alphafold-model-configuration-and-execution-alphafold-model-loading-and-jit-compilation)\. This involves converting parameters into a format compatible with the Haiku neural network library and configuring JAX Just\-In\-Time \(JIT\) compilation for optimal performance\. The system specifically optimizes compilation by identifying structurally unique model architectures and compiling each only once, then reusing these compiled instances with swapped parameters for other models with similar structures\.

 To ensure proper academic attribution, the pipeline automates the generation of BibTeX citations\. The [citations\.py L122](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/citations.py#L122) function in [`colabfold/citations.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/citations.py) dynamically selects and generates BibTeX entries based on the specific models and features utilized during a prediction run\. This includes citations for the core AlphaFold models, MMseqs2 for MSA generation, environmental databases, template usage, and Amber relaxation\. This ensures that users can easily cite the scientific methods and datasets that underpinned their protein structure predictions\.### AlphaFold3 Specific Integrations

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The pipeline integrates specific utilities to support AlphaFold3, facilitating broader molecular complex predictions beyond proteins\. This support includes the generation of AlphaFold3\-compatible input dictionaries and the handling of various molecule types\.

 A core function in [`colabfold/batch.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py), [batch\.py L1705](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1705), is responsible for processing queries and constructing a JSON file that contains all necessary inputs for AlphaFold3\. This JSON output includes MSA data and information for additional molecules, formatted specifically for AlphaFold3 compatibility\. The system also supports including non\-protein molecules like DNA, RNA, and ligands specified by SMILES strings or Chemical Component Dictionary \(CCD\) codes within the FASTA input, as detailed in [`README.md`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md)\.

 The utility functions for this integration are primarily found in [`colabfold/utils.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/utils.py)\. This file defines the [utils\.py L286](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/utils.py#L286) Enum, which classifies different molecule types\. The [utils\.py L309](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/utils.py#L309) class within this module is responsible for constructing AlphaFold3 input dictionaries using functions like [utils\.py L333](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/utils.py#L333) and [utils\.py L371](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/utils.py#L371), while also managing chain IDs to ensure proper formatting for AlphaFold3\. This comprehensive approach allows the pipeline to predict structures for diverse molecular complexes\. The [search\.py L34](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L34) function in [`colabfold/mmseqs/search.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py) also plays a role in this, supporting [batch\.py L2230](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L2230) generation\.## AlphaFold Model Configuration and Execution

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold model configuration and execution within this repository encompass the entire process of generating protein structure predictions, from preparing input features to running the models and analyzing the outputs\. This pipeline supports both AlphaFold and AlphaFold\-Multimer models\.

 The prediction workflow is managed by functions that prepare input features, generate Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\), and execute the AlphaFold models\. Input sequences are processed and formatted, with specialized handling for homooligomeric definitions\. MSA generation can leverage various methods, including [README\.md?plain=1 L9](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L9) and [README\.md?plain=1 L9](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L9), or use precomputed MSAs\. For protein complexes, a crucial step involves pairing MSAs to accurately represent multi\-chain interactions\. The system can trim specific residue ranges from sequences and filter MSA entries based on coverage and sequence identity\. Once prepared, the raw sequence and MSA data are transformed into AlphaFold\-compatible feature dictionaries, incorporating considerations for homooligomers and chain breaks\. The core prediction execution involves loading and configuring AlphaFold models with settings for parameters such as the number of recycles and ensembles, and then running the prediction\. The results are parsed to extract quality metrics like predicted lDDT \(pLDDT\), predicted TM\-score \(pTM\), and predicted aligned error \(PAE\)\. PDB files of the predicted structures are saved, and various plots are generated for visualization\. For a detailed breakdown of the workflow, refer to [Overall Workflow and Batch Processing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#protein-structure-prediction-pipeline-overall-workflow-and-batch-processing)\.

 Model weights are managed by loading pre\-trained Haiku parameters from [models\.py L49](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/models.py#L49) files for specific model types \(e\.g\., "alphafold2\_multimer\_v1", "alphafold2\_ptm"\)\. To optimize performance and reduce JAX compilation time, the system identifies structurally distinct model architectures and compiles only those\. For models sharing an architecture, an already compiled model runner is reused, and only the parameters are swapped\. This avoids redundant Just\-In\-Time \(JIT\) compilations, which can be computationally intensive\. This process is handled within the [models\.py L78](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/models.py#L78) function found in [`colabfold/alphafold/models.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/models.py)\.

 After prediction, the system provides advanced structural metric calculations and visualization tools\. It can compute predicted TM\-score variants, including interface predicted TM\-score \(ipTM\) and a modified version \(actifpTM\) that accounts for contact probabilities\. These metrics are used to assess inter\-chain and intra\-chain interactions within predicted protein complexes\. The results are visualized using matrix plots that display [extra\_ptm\.py L232](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L232) \(chain pTM\) on the diagonal, [extra\_ptm\.py L270](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L270) on the lower triangle, and [extra\_ptm\.py L270](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L270) on the upper triangle, offering a comprehensive view of model quality and interaction confidence\. The functions for these calculations are located in [`colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py)\.### AlphaFold Model Loading and JIT Compilation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The ColabFold pipeline manages the loading and configuration of AlphaFold models, including both AlphaFold and AlphaFold\-Multimer variants, and optimizes their execution through JAX Just\-In\-Time \(JIT\) compilation\. This process is orchestrated by the functions within [`colabfold/alphafold/models.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/models.py)\.

 The system identifies different model architectures and compiles them efficiently\. Instead of compiling a new model for every variation, it leverages the fact that only a few models \(e\.g\., AlphaFold model 1 and model 3\) possess structurally distinct configurations\. For other models, it reuses an already compiled instance and simply swaps in the relevant parameters\. This strategy significantly reduces compilation time, which is crucial given the complexity of AlphaFold models\.

 Configuration settings, such as the number of recycles, ensemble size, and the use of bfloat16 precision, are dynamically applied to the model before compilation\. JIT compilation itself is optimized for different performance modes—[README\.md?plain=1 L122](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L122), [README\.md?plain=1 L250](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L250), and [README\.md?plain=1 L130](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L130)—with specific settings for GPU GEMM operations\. These modes allow users to balance compilation speed with execution performance, tailoring the pipeline to available hardware and desired efficiency\. The system also handles the conversion of downloaded model parameters from [models\.py L49](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/models.py#L49) files into a format compatible with the Haiku neural network library, which is used by AlphaFold\.

 The ultimate goal is to provide optimized [batch\.py L345](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L345) instances, ready for protein structure prediction, while minimizing overhead associated with model setup and compilation\.### AlphaFold Input Feature Engineering and Preprocessing

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Creating AlphaFold\-compatible feature dictionaries involves a series of transformations that convert raw input sequences and Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) into the fixed\-size numerical inputs required by the AlphaFold models\. This process is crucial for enabling the models to interpret and predict protein structures\.

 A key step in this process is handling homooligomerization, where [colabfold\.py L271](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L271) within [`beta/colabfold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py) expands MSAs and deletion matrices to correctly represent complexes composed of multiple identical protein chains\. This function duplicates sequences and adjusts gaps according to specified copy numbers and chain lengths\.

 For multi\-chain predictions, [`beta/colabfold_alphafold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold_alphafold.py) leverages the [colabfold\.py L339](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L339) utility to define artificial chain breaks, allowing AlphaFold to model protein complexes effectively\. This involves modifying residue indices to signal boundaries between different polypeptide chains\.

 MSAs themselves undergo significant processing\. For multi\-sequence inputs, [pairmsa\.py L201](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/pairmsa.py#L201) within [`beta/pairmsa.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/pairmsa.py) combines individual MSAs into "paired" MSAs\. This stitching process identifies and aligns related sequences from different MSAs, which is particularly important for accurate predictions of protein complexes\. This involves sophisticated filtering steps to remove redundant sequences after stitching\. Further details on this process can be found in [MSA and Template Generation with MMseqs2](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#msa-and-template-generation-with-mmseqs2)\.

 Finally, all input features are converted into fixed\-size inputs\. This ensures consistency for the AlphaFold model, as varying input sizes would necessitate costly recompilations\. The [msa\.py L12](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/msa.py#L12) function within [`colabfold/alphafold/msa.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/msa.py) handles this by padding arrays within the feature dictionaries to predefined dimensions using zero\-padding\. This process is crucial for the efficient execution of AlphaFold models, especially in environments like JAX/XLA that benefit from static input shapes\.### Advanced Structural Metric Calculation and Visualization

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Predicted TM\-score \(pTM\) and its variants, such as interface predicted TM\-score \(ipTM\) and [batch\.py L539](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L539), are crucial metrics for evaluating the quality of predicted protein structures, especially for complexes\. These scores leverage the predicted aligned error \(PAE\) output from AlphaFold models to assess structural similarity both within individual protein chains and at the interfaces between interacting chains\. The core function, [extra\_ptm\.py L42](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L42) in [`colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py), calculates a predicted TM\-score using PAE logits and error bins\. This function can be configured with residue weights and pair residue weights, and it can also apply a [extra\_ptm\.py L89](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L89) to exclude intra\-chain residue pairs, which is essential for ipTM\-like calculations\.

 For inter\-chain interactions, [extra\_ptm\.py L206](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L206) in [`colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py) computes the standard ipTM between specified chains\. A more advanced metric, [batch\.py L539](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L539), is calculated by [extra\_ptm\.py L122](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L122) or [extra\_ptm\.py L163](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L163), which utilizes contact probabilities or binary contacts, respectively, to assess the confidence of interactions between chains\. Intra\-chain quality is evaluated by [extra\_ptm\.py L221](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L221), which calculates the pTM for individual chains\.

 The overall orchestration of these calculations is handled by [extra\_ptm\.py L251](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L251) in [`colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py), which iterates through all unique chain pairs to compute [extra\_ptm\.py L270](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L270), [extra\_ptm\.py L270](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L270), and [extra\_ptm\.py L270](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L270) values, along with a global [AlphaFold2\.ipynb L247](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/AlphaFold2.ipynb#L247)\. The results are visualized using [extra\_ptm\.py L331](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L331), which generates a matrix plot where the diagonal displays [extra\_ptm\.py L232](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L232), the lower triangle shows [extra\_ptm\.py L270](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L270), and the upper triangle represents [extra\_ptm\.py L270](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L270), providing a comprehensive view of complex prediction quality\. Contact maps, another essential visualization, are derived from distogram logits by [extra\_ptm\.py L22](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py#L22) in [`colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/extra_ptm.py), which sums probabilities for distances below a specified threshold\. These metrics and visualizations are critical for interpreting AlphaFold's output and gaining insights into the predicted protein\-protein interactions\.## MSA and Template Generation with MMseqs2

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [`colabfold/mmseqs`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs) directory provides functionality for generating and processing Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) and identifying template hits using the MMseqs2 software\. This is a preliminary step for protein structure prediction, enabling AlphaFold to leverage evolutionary information and structural homologous\.

 The process supports both monomeric and multimeric protein sequences\. For single protein sequences, a series of MMseqs2 commands search various databases, including UniRef and metagenomic databases, generating a comprehensive MSA and optional template hits\. This workflow is managed by the [search\.py L50](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L50) function in [`colabfold/mmseqs/search.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py)\. For multimeric protein sequences, specialized MMseqs2 workflows employ [search\.py L29](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L29) commands to produce paired MSAs, which are used for predicting protein complexes\. The [search\.py L212](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L212) function in [`colabfold/mmseqs/search.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py) handles this, searching against databases like [search\.py L53](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L53) or [search\.py L216](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L216)\.

 Beyond generation, the system includes utilities for managing A3M \(Alignments in Stockholm format\) files\. The [merge\_and\_split\_msas\.py L15](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/merge_and_split_msas.py#L15) function in [`colabfold/mmseqs/merge_and_split_msas.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/merge_and_split_msas.py) combines two A3M files into a single, merged file\. The [split\_msas\.py L14](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/split_msas.py#L14) function in [`colabfold/mmseqs/merge_and_split_msas.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/merge_and_split_msas.py) splits this merged file back into individual A3M files, one for each MSA\. Similarly, the [split\_msas\.py L14](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/split_msas.py#L14) function in [`colabfold/mmseqs/split_msas.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/split_msas.py) can split any multi\-MSA A3M file into separate files, aiding in the organization and processing of large datasets\. The overall orchestration, including argument parsing and calling the appropriate search functions, is handled by the [batch\.py L1771](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1771) function within [`colabfold/mmseqs/search.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py), which also supports generating AlphaFold3 input files\. The execution of individual MMseqs2 commands is abstracted by the [search\.py L34](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L34) helper function, which logs commands and avoids redundant operations\.### MMseqs2 Monomeric MSA and Template Search

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The process of generating Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) and template hits for single protein sequences using MMseqs2 is managed by the [search\.py L50](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L50) function in [`colabfold/mmseqs/search.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py)\. This function orchestrates a series of MMseqs2 commands to perform comprehensive searches against various databases, ultimately yielding a [search\.py L2](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L2) file containing the MSA and, optionally, template hits\.

 The workflow begins by preparing a query database \([colabfold\_search\.sh L36](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold_search.sh#L36)\) from the input protein sequences\. MMseqs2 then executes a series of steps:

 - A primary search \([README\.md?plain=1 L189](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L189)\) is conducted against the [search\.py L53](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L53) to find homologous sequences\.
- The search results are moved \([setup\_databases\.sh L2](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/setup_databases.sh#L2)\) and linked \([colabfold\_search\.sh L7](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold_search.sh#L7)\) to facilitate further processing\.
- Alignments are expanded \([colabfold\_search\.sh L7](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold_search.sh#L7)\) and then aligned more precisely \([README\.md?plain=1 L5](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L5)\)\.
- Results are filtered \([colabfold\_search\.sh L7](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold_search.sh#L7)\) to ensure quality and relevance\.
- Finally, the filtered results are converted into an MSA format \([colabfold\_search\.sh L7](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold_search.sh#L7)\)\.

 This process can also incorporate environmental databases \([search\.py L55](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L55)\) and template databases \([search\.py L54](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L54)\) when enabled, enriching the MSA with diverse sequence information and identifying potential structural templates\. The execution of each MMseqs2 command is managed by the [search\.py L34](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L34) helper function within [`colabfold/mmseqs/search.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py), which ensures commands are only run if their output does not already exist, preventing redundant computations\. The overall workflow, including command\-line argument parsing and temporary file cleanup, is handled by the [batch\.py L1771](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1771) function in [`colabfold/mmseqs/search.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py)\. For multimeric protein sequences, a specialized workflow exists, detailed in [MMseqs2 Multimeric MSA Generation for Protein Complexes](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#msa-and-template-generation-with-mmseqs2-mmseqs2-multimeric-msa-generation-for-protein-complexes)\.### MMseqs2 Multimeric MSA Generation for Protein Complexes

```
def mmseqs_search_pair(...): # parameters as in source
    # ... (preliminary checks and parameter setup)

    if pair_env:
        db = spire_db
        output = ".env.paired.a3m"
    else:
        db = uniref_db
        output = ".paired.a3m"

    # Common search parameters (sensitivity, GPU, etc.)
    search_param = ["--num-iterations", "3", "--db-load-mode", str(db_load_mode)]
    # ... (add other search_param elements)

    # Run MMseqs2 search command
    run_mmseqs(mmseqs, [
        "search", base.joinpath("qdb"), dbbase.joinpath(db), base.joinpath("res"),
        base.joinpath("tmp"), "--threads", str(threads),
    ] + search_param)

    # ... (various MMseqs2 expandaln, align, pairaln, and filterresult steps)

    # Generate final paired MSA (pair.a3m)
    run_mmseqs(mmseqs, [
        "result2msa", base.joinpath("qdb"), dbbase.joinpath(f"{db}{dbSuffix1}"),
        base.joinpath("res_final"), base.joinpath("pair.a3m"), "--db-load-mode",
        str(db_load_mode), "--msa-format-mode", "5", "--threads", str(threads),
    ] + filter_param)

    if unpack:
        # Unpack the generated 'pair.a3m' to a loose file named by 'output'
        run_mmseqs(mmseqs, [
            "unpackdb", base.joinpath("pair.a3m"), base.joinpath("."),
            "--unpack-name-mode", "0", "--unpack-suffix", output,
        ])
        run_mmseqs(mmseqs, ["rmdb", base.joinpath("pair.a3m")])

    # ... (cleanup of intermediate MMseqs2 databases)
```

The process of generating Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) for multimeric protein sequences in ColabFold utilizes specialized MMseqs2 workflows to enable the prediction of protein complexes\. This involves focusing on the [search\.py L29](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L29) commands, which are crucial for producing paired MSAs\. These paired MSAs are essential for accurately modeling the interactions within a complex, as they align sequences from multiple protein chains simultaneously, capturing their evolutionary co\-variation\.

 The function responsible for orchestrating these searches is [search\.py L212](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L212) within [`colabfold/mmseqs/search.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py)\. This function employs specific MMseqs2 operations to search against databases like [search\.py L53](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L53) or a specialized pairing environmental database \([search\.py L216](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L216)\)\. The choice of database depends on whether environmental sequences are included \([search\.py L218](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L218) parameter\)\. The output of this process is a [search\.py L251](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L251) or [search\.py L248](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L248) file, which contains the MSA information structured to support multimeric predictions\. The system supports various databases and integrates [search\.py L47](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/search.py#L47) for executing MMseqs2 commands while managing logging and avoiding redundant operations\. For a general overview of MMseqs2 MSA and template generation, refer to [MSA and Template Generation with MMseqs2](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#msa-and-template-generation-with-mmseqs2)\.### Merging and Splitting A3M Files

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [README\.md?plain=1 L1](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L1) repository includes utilities for manipulating A3M \(Alignments in Stockholm format\) files, which are central to handling Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\)\. These utilities facilitate the merging of multiple MSAs into a single file and the subsequent splitting of such combined files back into individual A3M files\. This process is crucial for managing and processing large sets of sequence alignments, particularly in the context of protein structure prediction workflows\.

 The primary merging operation combines two specific A3M files, typically [colabfold\.py L180](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L180) and [colabfold\.py L181](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L181), into a single [merge\_and\_split\_msas\.py L21](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/merge_and_split_msas.py#L21) file\. This merging is performed using an external [README\.md?plain=1 L37](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L37) tool, which is invoked via a dedicated function in [`colabfold/mmseqs/merge_and_split_msas.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/merge_and_split_msas.py)\. The [README\.md?plain=1 L37](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L37) command handles the database merging, resulting in a single file where individual MSAs are delimited by null characters \([split\_msas\.py L22](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/split_msas.py#L22)\)\.

 Following the merge, or independently for any multi\-MSA A3M file, the system provides functionality to split the combined A3M file\. The [split\_msas\.py L14](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/split_msas.py#L14) function, located in [`colabfold/mmseqs/merge_and_split_msas.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/merge_and_split_msas.py) and [`colabfold/mmseqs/split_msas.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/mmseqs/split_msas.py), reads the merged file, identifies each individual MSA by its null character delimiter, and writes each into a separate A3M file within a specified output directory\. The filename for each newly created A3M file is derived from the first line of the MSA, ensuring a meaningful and traceable naming convention\. This splitting process allows for individual processing or storage of each MSA, avoiding the need to load very large combined files into memory\. This functionality is part of the broader [MSA and Template Generation with MMseqs2](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#msa-and-template-generation-with-mmseqs2) process\.## Local MSA Server Setup and Management

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

A local ColabFold API server can be established and managed for efficient Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) generation\. This server automates the download of necessary binaries and databases, handles compilation, and manages service startup\. This setup allows for the generation of MSAs without relying on external services, which can be beneficial for performance and data privacy\.

 The setup process begins with the execution of the [README\.md?plain=1 L5](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L5) script, located in [`MsaServer/setup-and-start-local.sh`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/setup-and-start-local.sh)\. This script verifies system dependencies such as [Contributing\.md?plain=1 L6](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/Contributing.md?plain=1#L6), [Boltz1\.ipynb L259](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/Boltz1.ipynb#L259), [setup\_databases\.sh L7](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/setup_databases.sh#L7), and [setup\_databases\.sh L9](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/setup_databases.sh#L9)\. It then automatically downloads specific versions of [README\.md?plain=1 L37](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L37) and [README\.md?plain=1 L10](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L10) binaries, tailoring them to the detected operating system and architecture \(e\.g\., Linux x86\_64/arm64, macOS universal\)\. Database acquisition is also handled by this script, fetching [batch\.py L1795](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1795) and [README\.md?plain=1 L11](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L11)\. The script is designed to be idempotent, meaning it can be run multiple times without causing issues, as it skips steps for components that are already up to date\. Users can configure the PDB mirror server and enable GPU mode for enhanced performance\.

 Server configurations, such as the bind address, port, and the number of local job workers, are managed through the [batch\.py L1382](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1382) file\. This allows for customization of the server's operational parameters\. For optimal performance, especially when using the server in CPU mode, it is recommended to load the search databases entirely into system memory\. The [README\.md?plain=1 L130](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L130) utility can be employed for this purpose, though it requires substantial RAM \(768GB\-1024GB for [batch\.py L1795](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1795) and [README\.md?plain=1 L11](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L11)\)\.

 For continuous and robust operation, the local MSA server can be integrated as a system service, typically using [README\.md?plain=1 L44](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L44)\. Management of this service, including stopping, clearing job data, and restarting, is facilitated by the [`MsaServer/restart-systemd.sh`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/restart-systemd.sh) script\. This ensures that the server can be maintained efficiently and its job data cleared as needed\. Once the server is running, [pyproject\.toml L56](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/pyproject.toml#L56) or notebook environments can specify the local server's URL using the [utils\.py L33](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/utils.py#L33) argument or a [mock\.py L165](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L165) parameter, respectively\.### Automated Server Setup and Dependency Management

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [`MsaServer/setup-and-start-local.sh`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/setup-and-start-local.sh) script automates the preparation and launch of a local ColabFold API server, designed for efficient Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) generation\. This script ensures that the necessary dependencies are present, retrieves platform\-specific binaries, downloads crucial databases, compiles the API server, and initiates its operation\.

 The script begins by performing dependency checks, verifying the availability of essential tools like [Contributing\.md?plain=1 L6](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/Contributing.md?plain=1#L6), [Boltz1\.ipynb L259](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/Boltz1.ipynb#L259), [setup\_databases\.sh L7](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/setup_databases.sh#L7), and [setup\_databases\.sh L9](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/setup_databases.sh#L9)\. It then dynamically determines the system's architecture and operating system to download the correct [README\.md?plain=1 L37](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L37) and [README\.md?plain=1 L10](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L10) binaries\. These binaries are retrieved from designated sources, with specific identifiers ensuring version consistency\.

 A critical phase involves the setup of protein databases\. The script creates a [README\.md?plain=1 L36](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L36) directory and utilizes an external script, [`setup_databases.sh`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/setup_databases.sh), to download and prepare [batch\.py L1795](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1795) and [README\.md?plain=1 L11](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L11)\. Users can select a PDB mirror and configure GPU usage if supported\. For testing purposes, a [setup\_databases\.sh L76](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/setup_databases.sh#L76) flag allows for the use of a smaller, more manageable database\.

 Upon successful preparation, the script compiles the API server and initiates the [README\.md?plain=1 L10](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L10) in local mode, using settings defined in [batch\.py L1382](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1382)\. The design emphasizes idempotency, meaning that repeated executions of the script will only perform steps that are necessary, such as updating out\-of\-date components, rather than re\-executing all setup procedures from scratch\. This approach streamlines maintenance and ensures that the server environment remains consistent and up\-to\-date\. Further details on managing this server, including system service integration and performance tuning, are available in [Local MSA Server Setup and Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#local-msa-server-setup-and-management)\.### Performance Optimization and Memory Configuration

Optimal performance of the local ColabFold API server, particularly for Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) searches, heavily relies on the rapid accessibility of its search databases\. To achieve response times typically measured in seconds, these databases must reside entirely within system memory rather than being accessed from slower disk storage\. The utility [README\.md?plain=1 L130](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L130) is employed to facilitate this by forcing the database files into the system's memory cache\.

 It is important to note the substantial memory requirements associated with this approach\. When operating in CPU mode, the standard [batch\.py L1795](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1795) and [README\.md?plain=1 L11](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L11) databases collectively demand between 768GB and 1024GB of RAM to be fully loaded into memory\. This memory allocation is critical for preventing disk I/O bottlenecks during MSA generation\. The [`MsaServer/README.md`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md) provides further guidance on how to use [README\.md?plain=1 L130](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L130) for this purpose\.### System Service Integration and Management

```
[Unit]
Description=ColabFold API Server
After=network.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/path/to/your/setup-and-start-local.sh  # Adjust path to your script
WorkingDirectory=/path/to/colabfold_msa_server     # Adjust to your server directory
Environment="GPU=1"                                # Uncomment to enable GPU mode
Environment="DEBUG_MINI_DB=1"                      # Optional: For quick tests with mini DB
Restart=always
RestartSec=10

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

For robust operation and automatic management of the ColabFold API server, especially in production environments, integration with system services is crucial\. This typically involves using a process supervisor like [README\.md?plain=1 L44](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L44) to ensure the server starts automatically at boot, restarts upon failure, and can be easily managed\.

 The repository provides an example [README\.md?plain=1 L44](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L44) service configuration, [README\.md?plain=1 L48](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L48), which serves as a template for setting up the ColabFold API server as a system service\. After the initial setup using [README\.md?plain=1 L5](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L5), this example configuration can be adapted to specify the correct paths for the server binary and its working directory\. Once configured, standard [README\.md?plain=1 L44](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L44) commands can be used to enable and start the service, ensuring that the ColabFold API server operates reliably in the background\.

 To facilitate management of the [README\.md?plain=1 L44](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L44) service and its associated data, the [README\.md?plain=1 L49](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L49) script is provided\. This script offers a convenient way to perform a controlled restart of the [README\.md?plain=1 L10](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/MsaServer/README.md?plain=1#L10) service\. Its key function is to stop the service, clear any existing job data by removing and recreating the [utils\.py L31](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/utils.py#L31) directory, and then restart the server\. This ensures a clean slate for new processing tasks and helps in troubleshooting by eliminating stale data\. More details on the automated setup process can be found in [Automated Server Setup and Dependency Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#local-msa-server-setup-and-management-automated-server-setup-and-dependency-management)\.## DeepFold Model Weight Conversion Utility

```
# Simplified example of DeepFold to AlphaFold weight key renaming
# This snippet focuses on the key transformation logic.

# Example of a DeepFold-style weight dictionary (stubbed for brevity)
# In reality, this would be loaded from a .npz file.
tmp_params = {
    'deepfold_model/layer_0': {
        'weights': '...',
        'biases': '...'
    },
    'alphafold_batch/embedding': { # Example of a key that also needs 'alphafold_batch/' removed
        'embedding_weights': '...'
    },
    'deepfold_other/attention': {
        'q_proj': '...'
    }
}

params = {}
for k, v in tmp_params.items():
    for i, j in v.items():
        # The core renaming logic:
        # 1. Replace 'deepfold' with 'alphafold'
        # 2. Remove 'alphafold_batch/' prefix
        # 3. Concatenate the original outer and inner keys with '//'
        new_key = k.replace('deepfold', 'alphafold').replace('alphafold_batch/', '') + '//' + i
        params[new_key] = j # Storing the value (actual weights)

# Example of how the new keys would look
# print(params.keys())
# Expected output (simplified):
# dict_keys(['alphafold_model/layer_0//weights', 'alphafold_model/layer_0//biases',
#            'embedding//embedding_weights', 'alphafold_other/attention//q_proj'])
```

The utility in [`utils`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/utils) provides a mechanism for converting DeepFold model weights into a format compatible with AlphaFold\. This conversion is crucial for interoperability, allowing DeepFold\-trained models to be used within the AlphaFold prediction pipeline\. The core of this functionality lies in systematically renaming the keys within the weight files and subsequently saving these transformed weights into a new NumPy archive\. This process ensures that the parameter names align with AlphaFold's expected structure, facilitating their correct loading and use in subsequent prediction steps\. The conversion is handled by the script [`utils/convert_deepfold_weights.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/utils/convert_deepfold_weights.py)\.### DeepFold to AlphaFold Key Renaming Logic

```
# tmp_params is loaded from the input .npz file
# tmp_params = np.load(sys.argv[1], allow_pickle=True)['arr_0'].flat[0]
params = {}
tmp_params = {
    'deepfold/model/key1': {
        'subkey_a': ..., # example value
        'subkey_b': ...,
    },
    'alphafold_batch/model/key2': {
        'subkey_c': ...,
    },
    'deepfold/another_module/key3': {
        'subkey_d': ...,
    }
}

for k, v in tmp_params.items():
    for i, j in v.items():
        # Illustrates key renaming: deepfold -> alphafold, removes alphafold_batch/, adds //
        new_key = k.replace('deepfold', 'alphafold').replace('alphafold_batch/', '') + '//' + i
        params[new_key] = j

# Example of how 'params' would look after transformation:
# params = {
#     'alphafold/model/key1//subkey_a': ...,
#     'alphafold/model/key1//subkey_b': ...,
#     'model/key2//subkey_c': ...,
#     'alphafold/another_module/key3//subkey_d': ...,
# }
# np.savez(sys.argv[2], **params)
```

The conversion utility handles DeepFold model weights to ensure their compatibility with AlphaFold\. This process involves a specific key renaming scheme\. The system identifies keys containing 'deepfold' and replaces this string with 'alphafold'\. Additionally, the prefix 'alphafold\_batch/' is removed from the keys\. To further align with AlphaFold's expected weight format, the original inner key is appended with [utils\.py L330](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/utils.py#L330) to the modified key\. This structured renaming ensures that the converted weights are correctly interpreted and utilized by AlphaFold models\. For further details on the conversion process, see [DeepFold Model Weight Conversion Utility](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#deepfold-model-weight-conversion-utility)\.### Saving Converted Weights as NumPy Archives

```
# tmp_params would be loaded from a deepfold weights file
tmp_params = {
    'deepfold_model/key1': {'param_a': np.array([1, 2]), 'param_b': np.array([3, 4])},
    'alphafold_batch/key2': {'param_c': np.array([5, 6])}
}

params = {}
for k, v in tmp_params.items():
    for i, j in v.items():
        # Keys are transformed to match alphafold naming conventions
        new_key = k.replace('deepfold', 'alphafold').replace('alphafold_batch/', '') + '//' + i
        params[new_key] = j

# The 'params' dictionary now contains transformed keys
# For example: 'alphafold_model/key1//param_a' : np.array([1, 2])

# Save the transformed weights to a NumPy archive file
# sys.argv[2] would be the output file path
np.savez("alphafold_weights.npz", **params)
```

After the DeepFold model weights are transformed into an AlphaFold\-compatible structure, they are persistently stored for future use\. The utility script handles this by saving the newly constructed dictionary of weights to a NumPy archive\. This process utilizes the [convert\_deepfold\_weights\.py L9](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/utils/convert_deepfold_weights.py#L9) function, which creates a [models\.py L49](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/alphafold/models.py#L49) file containing multiple arrays, each identified by a key corresponding to the parameter name\. This ensures that the converted model weights are readily available and can be loaded efficiently by AlphaFold for subsequent predictions, maintaining the integrity and structure of the parameters\. The conversion utility is implemented in [`utils/convert_deepfold_weights.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/utils/convert_deepfold_weights.py)\.## Stereo\-chemical Properties and Reference Data

Reference data concerning the stereo\-chemical properties of amino acids are integral for molecular modeling and validation within the protein structure prediction pipeline\. This data ensures that predicted structures adhere to established geometric parameters, enhancing their realism and accuracy\.

 The primary source for these properties is the [AlphaFold2\_advanced\.ipynb L398](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/AlphaFold2_advanced.ipynb#L398) file located in [`colabfold/openstructure`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure)\. This file contains empirical data derived from crystallographic tables, specifically a publication by Engh RA and Huber R\. It is organized into sections detailing bond lengths, bond angles, and non\-bonded distances, complete with mean values and standard deviations for various amino acid residues\. These parameters are crucial for assessing the quality and plausibility of predicted protein structures by comparing modeled geometries against experimentally determined standards\. For instance, the "Bond" section provides expected covalent bond lengths \(e\.g\., [stereo\_chemical\_props\.txt L2](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/stereo_chemical_props.txt#L2), [stereo\_chemical\_props\.txt L3](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/stereo_chemical_props.txt#L3)\), while the "Angle" section details typical bond angles \(e\.g\., [stereo\_chemical\_props\.txt L158](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/stereo_chemical_props.txt#L158)\)\. The "Non\-bonded distance" section includes minimum distances and tolerances between different atom types to help identify potential steric clashes\.

 The data provided in [AlphaFold2\_advanced\.ipynb L398](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/AlphaFold2_advanced.ipynb#L398) is distributed under the GNU Lesser General Public License v3\.0, as indicated in [`colabfold/openstructure/README.md`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/README.md) and detailed in [`colabfold/openstructure/LGPL.txt`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/LGPL.txt)\. This licensing ensures its free use, modification, and distribution under specified conditions\.### Data Source and Licensing for Stereo\-chemical Properties
