The stereo\-chemical property data used in this repository originates from the [RoseTTAFold\.ipynb L129](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/RoseTTAFold.ipynb#L129) project\. The numerical data itself, detailing bond lengths, bond angles, and non\-bonded distances, is derived from the publication by Engh RA and Huber R in "International Tables for Crystallography\. Vol\. F"\. This dataset is distributed under the GNU Lesser General Public License v3\.0, as indicated in [`colabfold/openstructure/README.md`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/README.md) and detailed in [`colabfold/openstructure/LGPL.txt`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/LGPL.txt)\. The [AlphaFold2\_advanced\.ipynb L398](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/AlphaFold2_advanced.ipynb#L398) file within [`colabfold/openstructure`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure) contains these parameters, which are crucial for validating and refining molecular models\. For a detailed structure and application of these parameters, refer to [Structure and Application of Stereo\-chemical Parameters](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#stereo-chemical-properties-and-reference-data-structure-and-application-of-stereo-chemical-parameters)\.### Structure and Application of Stereo\-chemical Parameters

The [AlphaFold2\_advanced\.ipynb L398](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/AlphaFold2_advanced.ipynb#L398) file, located in [`colabfold/openstructure/stereo_chemical_props.txt`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/stereo_chemical_props.txt), provides empirical data on the stereo\-chemical properties of amino acids\. This data is structured into three main categories: bond lengths, bond angles, and non\-bonded distances\. Each entry within these categories specifies a [stereo\_chemical\_props\.txt L1](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/stereo_chemical_props.txt#L1) type, a [AlphaFold3\_of3\.ipynb L482](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/AlphaFold3_of3.ipynb#L482) value, and a [stereo\_chemical\_props\.txt L1](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/stereo_chemical_props.txt#L1) \(standard deviation\) for the respective geometric parameter\. For non\-bonded distances, a [stereo\_chemical\_props\.txt L334](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/stereo_chemical_props.txt#L334) and [batch\.py L2009](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L2009) are provided instead\.

 This reference dataset is applied in molecular modeling, particularly for the validation and refinement of protein structures\. By comparing predicted or calculated geometric features of a polypeptide chain against these established empirical values, deviations can be identified\. For example, if a [stereo\_chemical\_props\.txt L2](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/stereo_chemical_props.txt#L2) bond in an Alanine residue in a predicted structure significantly deviates from the mean length \(1\.520 Å\) and standard deviation \(0\.021 Å\) specified in the "Bond" section of [AlphaFold2\_advanced\.ipynb L398](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/AlphaFold2_advanced.ipynb#L398), it may indicate an issue with the predicted structure\. Similarly, the non\-bonded distance data helps in detecting potential steric clashes, where two atoms are found closer than their specified [stereo\_chemical\_props\.txt L334](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/stereo_chemical_props.txt#L334) minus [batch\.py L2009](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L2009)\. This data is derived from the publication by Engh RA and Huber R in "International Tables for Crystallography\. Vol\. F" and is distributed under the GNU Lesser General Public License v3\.0, as noted in [`colabfold/openstructure/README.md`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/openstructure/README.md)\. For more details on the licensing, refer to [Data Source and Licensing for Stereo\-chemical Properties](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#stereo-chemical-properties-and-reference-data-data-source-and-licensing-for-stereo-chemical-properties)\.## Testing Utilities for Protein Structure Prediction

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

ColabFold employs a suite of testing utilities to ensure the reliability and correctness of its protein structure prediction pipeline\. This includes mock implementations for external dependencies, a notebook reformatting script, and comprehensive unit tests\.

 To facilitate stable and independent testing, especially given dependencies on external services and computationally intensive models, [README\.md?plain=1 L1](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L1) utilizes mock implementations\. The [mock\.py L44](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L44) class, found in [`tests/mock.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py), simulates the behavior of AlphaFold's prediction method\. It manages the storage and retrieval of expected prediction outcomes, allowing tests to run without invoking the actual AlphaFold model\. Similarly, the [mock\.py L126](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L126) class, within the same file, mimics the responses of the MMseqs2 API, enabling consistent testing of Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) generation without requiring live API calls\. These mocks support snapshot testing, where expected outputs are saved and compared against subsequent test runs\.

 Beyond functional testing, [README\.md?plain=1 L1](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L1) also includes a utility for maintaining code style\. The script [`tests/reindent_ipynb.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/reindent_ipynb.py) standardizes the JSON formatting of Jupyter notebooks, ensuring consistent indentation and character encoding for improved readability and version control\.

 The core testing framework for [README\.md?plain=1 L1](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L1) resides in unit tests designed to validate the pipeline's functionalities\. These tests, primarily located in [`tests/test_colabfold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/test_colabfold.py), [`tests/test_msa.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/test_msa.py), and [`tests/test_utils.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/test_utils.py), cover various aspects of the prediction process:

 - **Batch and Sequence Prediction**: Tests verify the correct execution of the main prediction function, including handling single sequences and batch processing, and ensuring the proper generation of output files such as PDBs and configuration data\.
- **Complex Prediction**: Different scenarios for predicting protein complexes, including homomultimers and heteromultimers, are tested, assessing the pipeline's ability to handle various multimer models and sequence configurations\.
- **MSA Handling**: Specific tests focus on the generation and serialization of MSAs, ensuring that the alignment data is correctly produced, stored, and deserialized\. These tests also validate the identification of complex types from input queries\. See [MSA and Template Generation with MMseqs2](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#msa-and-template-generation-with-mmseqs2) for more details\.
- **Input and Output Processing**: The pipeline's ability to parse diverse input formats \(e\.g\., FASTA, A3M, CSV\) and to convert and validate structural files \(PDB to mmCIF\) is also thoroughly tested\. See [Input Data Handling and Homooligomerization](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#protein-structure-prediction-pipeline-input-data-handling-and-homooligomerization) for more details on input handling\.

 The testing utilities collectively ensure that the [README\.md?plain=1 L1](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L1) pipeline operates predictably across different inputs and configurations while minimizing reliance on external services during the testing phase\.### Mocking External Dependencies for Stable Testing

```
class MMseqs2Mock:
  """Mocks out the call to the mmseqs2 api"""

  def __init__(self, rootpath: Path, name: str):
    self.data_file = ... # Path to the JSON file
    # Load saved responses from the JSON file
    with self.data_file.open() as fp:
      self.saved_responses = []
      for saved_response in json.load(fp):
        response = join_lines(saved_response["response"])
        self.saved_responses.append(
          {"config": saved_response["config"], "response": response}
        )

  def mock_run_mmseqs2(self, query, prefix, **kwargs):
    config = {
      "query": query,
      **kwargs # other configuration parameters
    }

    for saved_response in self.saved_responses:
      if saved_response["config"] == config:
        return saved_response["response"]

    if os.environ.get("UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS"):
      # If UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS is set, call the real run_mmseqs2
      # and save the response for future mock calls.
      response = run_mmseqs2(x=config["query"], prefix=prefix, **config)
      response = split_lines(response)
      self.saved_responses.append({"config": config, "response": response})
      self.data_file.write_text(json.dumps(self.saved_responses, indent=2))
    else:
      assert False, config # Raise an error if no matching response is found
```

The protein structure prediction pipeline incorporates mock implementations for external services to ensure stable and independent testing\. This approach avoids reliance on actual external network requests or complex AlphaFold model setups, which can be time\-consuming and resource\-intensive\. The primary mock components are [mock\.py L44](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L44) for AlphaFold prediction and [mock\.py L126](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L126) for MMseqs2 API calls, both defined in [`tests/mock.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py)\.

 The [mock\.py L44](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L44) class simulates the [mock\.py L59](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L59) method of [test\_colabfold\.py L53](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/test_colabfold.py#L53)\. It manages predictions using pre\-configured fixture directories and a sequence of expected prediction files\. This allows tests to either generate and save new predictions if they are missing or if a [mock\.py L73](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L73) environment variable is set, or to load previously saved features and predictions\. This mechanism supports snapshot testing, where expected outputs are stored and compared against current runs\. The [mock\.py L32](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L32) utility facilitates the conversion of JAX arrays to NumPy for serialization, and [mock\.py L19](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L19) addresses compatibility issues with JAX [mock\.py L21](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L21) during loading\.

 Similarly, the [mock\.py L126](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L126) class provides a mock for [test\_msa\.py L16](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/test_msa.py#L16), which handles interactions with the MMseqs2 API\. This mock uses a JSON file \([mock\.py L134](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L134)\) to store saved API responses\. When a request is made, [mock\.py L126](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L126) attempts to find a matching configuration in its saved responses\. If [mock\.py L131](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L131) is enabled and no match is found, it executes the actual [colabfold\.py L66](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/beta/colabfold.py#L66) function, records the input configuration and its response, and updates the JSON snapshot\. Otherwise, it returns the pre\-recorded response, ensuring consistent test outcomes without making live API calls\. Helper functions such as [mock\.py L213](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L213) and [mock\.py L223](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/mock.py#L223) are used to manage the storage and retrieval of multiline string responses within the JSON format\. Comprehensive unit tests, as detailed in [Unit Testing Framework for ColabFold Core Functionalities](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#testing-utilities-for-protein-structure-prediction-unit-testing-framework-for-colabfold-core-functionalities), leverage these mock implementations to validate various aspects of the prediction pipeline\.### Unit Testing Framework for ColabFold Core Functionalities

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [README\.md?plain=1 L1](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L1) repository employs a comprehensive unit testing strategy to ensure the reliability of its core functionalities\. This strategy focuses on verifying the behavior of the main [batch\.py L1189](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1189) function, which orchestrates the entire prediction pipeline, as well as distinct prediction scenarios and critical utility functions\.

 The tests are organized primarily within the [`tests`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests) directory\. The [`tests/test_colabfold.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/test_colabfold.py) file contains tests that cover the overall prediction workflow, including:

 - **Batch Processing and Single Sequence Prediction**: Tests validate the system's ability to process multiple protein sequences in a batch and predict the structure of individual sequences\. This includes checking the generation of output files and logs\.
- **Complex Prediction \(Multimers\)**: Various scenarios for predicting protein complexes, such as homomultimers and heteromultimers, are tested\. These tests ensure the correct application of different AlphaFold models \(e\.g\., [AlphaFold2\.ipynb L235](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/AlphaFold2.ipynb#L235), [AlphaFold2\.ipynb L235](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/AlphaFold2.ipynb#L235)\) and the accurate scoring of complex interactions\.
- **MSA Serialization**: Functions for converting Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) to and from string representations \([input\.py L75](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/input.py#L75) and [batch\.py L1001](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L1001)\) are tested\. This ensures the integrity of MSA data throughout the prediction pipeline, including the parsing of complex input queries via [input\.py L267](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/input.py#L267)\.

 Specific tests for MSA generation are found in [`tests/test_msa.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/test_msa.py), which focuses on the [batch\.py L648](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L648) function\. This function's role in retrieving MSAs and template features for various configurations is verified by simulating external [README\.md?plain=1 L9](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L9) calls using a mock object\.

 Furthermore, [`tests/test_utils.py`](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/tests/test_utils.py) is dedicated to testing utility functions crucial for input data handling and structural file management:

 - **Input Query Parsing**: The [input\.py L267](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/input.py#L267) function is tested for its ability to correctly parse diverse input formats, including FASTA, A3M, and CSV files\. This ensures that sequences are correctly extracted and categorized \(e\.g\., as part of a complex or a single chain\)\.
- **PDB to mmCIF Conversion**: The [batch\.py L210](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L210) function is tested to ensure accurate conversion of PDB files into the mmCIF format, including validation against AlphaFold's parsing capabilities\.
- **mmCIF Validation and Fixes**: The [batch\.py L172](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/colabfold/batch.py#L172) function is tested for its ability to identify and correct issues in mmCIF files, such as missing revision dates, and to raise errors for critically missing data\.

 These tests utilize mocking techniques, as detailed in [Mocking External Dependencies for Stable Testing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/sokrypton/colabfold#testing-utilities-for-protein-structure-prediction-mocking-external-dependencies-for-stable-testing), to isolate and test components without relying on external services or lengthy computations\. This allows for stable and efficient testing of the core [README\.md?plain=1 L1](https://github.com/sokrypton/colabfold/blob/d04bf9c8a9980807c270f9597c85ce754d9cd42b/README.md?plain=1#L1) functionalities\.
